description: GemPy is an open-source Python library for implicit 3D structural geological modelling, which interpolates surfaces, folds, faults and unconformities from points and orientation data and supports probabilistic modelling for uncertainty analysis. It is developed by the GemPy project community, whose original authors lead Terranigma Solutions GmbH, which maintains it and offers consulting. It is used worldwide for research and teaching in structural geology and for building subsurface models; GemPy version 3 was released in 2024. The code is on GitHub and free to install; GPU acceleration and automatic differentiation allow Bayesian inference, and results can be visualised in PyVista, Blender or LiquidEarth and linked with GemGIS, pyGIMLi and SimPEG. Caveats: the project page does not state the licence, and models depend heavily on the quality and density of the input geological observations. For simulation it gives the geometry and its uncertainty for subsurface models used in mining, tunnelling and geothermal hazard exposure studies, and ensembles of plausible geologies for probabilistic infrastructure risk assessment. It is related to the Leapfrog Geo record in this catalogue, a commercial implicit modeller, and the OpenGeoSys record, which simulates processes in such models.
